records.title: Social Security Act of 1935
records.billNumber: H.R. 7260 (enacted House bill; initial proposal numbers unverified)
sponsors: Robert Doughton and David Lewis (House proposal)
supporters: House: 284 Democrats and 81 Republicans voted yes; Senate: 60 Democrats and 16 Republicans voted yes
opponents: House: 15 Democrats and 15 Republicans voted no; Senate: 1 Democrat and 5 Republicans voted no
records.policyGoal: Federal old-age insurance and state assistance/unemployment compensation
records.argumentsFor: Economic security for vulnerable people during the Depression; federal support for state programs.
records.argumentsAgainst: Objections to federal intrusion and additional employer taxation.
records.amendments: Ways and Means renamed bill March 1; specific substantive amendment texts unverified.

records.title: Banking Act of 1933 (Glass-Steagall)
supporters: small rural banks supporting deposit insurance
opponents: Roosevelt initially threatened veto over deposit insurance
records.policyGoal: Separate banking functions and insure deposits
records.argumentsFor: Reduce speculative use of bank assets; protect depositors and smaller banks.
records.argumentsAgainst: Deposit insurance drew opposition including initial presidential veto threats.
records.amendments: Deposit insurance provision added to secure Steagall's support.
records.status: partially verified dossier; unverified fields remain

records.title: Veterans' adjusted compensation / bonus legislation (distinct bills)
sponsors: Wright Patman and Smith Brookhart (early-payment proposals)
opponents: Joseph T. Robinson and Reed Smoot (1932 early cash payment)
records.policyGoal: Compensate veterans and debate timing of payment
records.argumentsFor: Military pay lagged civilian earnings; unemployed veterans needed relief.
records.argumentsAgainst: Cost and fiscal balance; opponents questioned prioritizing veterans over other distressed citizens.
records.amendments: 1924 deferred certificates rather than immediate payment; further amendment text unverified.
records.finalDisposition: Separate 1924 deferred compensation and 1936 early redemption laws enacted; earlier proposals differed.
records.status: partially verified dossier; unverified fields remain

records.title: Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act
supporters: Protectionist legislators; Hoover signed the measure
records.policyGoal: Protect domestic producers through higher import tariffs
records.argumentsFor: Support domestic producers, particularly farmers facing low prices.
records.argumentsAgainst: Concern about retaliation and international trade contraction.

records.title: Judicial Reorganization Plan
records.policyGoal: Additional judges when older incumbent judges remain in office; Supreme Court could grow to fifteen
records.argumentsFor: Administration argued additional personnel and new judges would improve judicial efficiency.
records.argumentsAgainst: Senate Judiciary Committee argued the scheme threatened judicial independence and constitutional checks.
records.amendments: Committee amended measure and issued adverse recommendation; specific amendments unverified.
stages: adverse committee recommendation (report date per reproduced text)

records.title: Neutrality Acts of 1935 and 1939
opponents: Roosevelt initially opposed 1935 restrictions; Congress resisted earlier attempts at expanded cash-and-carry in 1939
records.policyGoal: Reduce involvement in foreign wars; revise restrictions as war expands
records.argumentsFor: Avoid entanglement and financial incentives for war; 1939 revision allowed trade without American shipping.
records.argumentsAgainst: Rigid embargo limited presidential flexibility and potential support for Britain and France.
records.amendments: 1936 loan prohibition; 1937 discretionary cash-and-carry for nonarms; 1939 arms embargo lifted.
records.finalDisposition: Both acts enacted; successive revisions changed restrictions.

records.title: Women's suffrage ratification certified
records.policyGoal: Secretary of State Bainbridge Colby certified ratification of the Nineteenth Amendment.

records.title: Emergency Quota Act signed
records.policyGoal: Harding signed a law restricting immigration through nationality-based quotas.

records.title: Emergency Tariff Act enacted
records.policyGoal: Temporary protective tariffs were imposed, particularly on agricultural imports.

records.title: Federal budget and auditing reorganized
records.policyGoal: The Budget and Accounting Act established executive budgeting and federal auditing institutions.

records.title: War with Germany formally ended
records.policyGoal: Harding signed a congressional joint resolution ending the state of war with Germany.

records.title: Maternal and infant health law enacted
records.policyGoal: The Sheppard-Towner Act provides federal matching funds for state maternal and infant health programs.
stages: Maternal and infant health law enacted

records.title: Farm cooperatives gain legal protection
records.policyGoal: The Capper-Volstead Act gives agricultural producers a limited antitrust exemption for cooperative marketing.

records.title: Cable Act signed
records.policyGoal: The Cable Act relaxed rules governing citizenship retention by American women marrying foreigners.

records.title: Coolidge outlines policy agenda
records.policyGoal: In his first State of the Union message, Coolidge supported tax reductions and Prohibition.

records.title: Immigration quotas tightened
records.policyGoal: A new immigration law tightened national-origin quotas and barred Japanese immigration.

records.title: Coolidge signs Revenue Act
records.policyGoal: Coolidge signed a Revenue Act reducing federal income taxes and other levies.

records.title: Air Commerce Act approved
records.policyGoal: The Air Commerce Act gives the Commerce Department regulatory authority over pilots and aircraft.

records.title: Pact renouncing war signed in Paris
records.policyGoal: Fifteen countries, including the United States, signed the Kellogg-Briand Pact renouncing war as national policy.

records.title: Agricultural Marketing Act signed
records.policyGoal: Hoover signed legislation establishing a Federal Farm Board to support farm cooperatives.

records.title: Veterans' administration law signed
records.policyGoal: Hoover signed legislation authorizing consolidation of federal veterans' benefit agencies.

records.title: Reconstruction Finance Corporation authorized
records.policyGoal: Hoover signed legislation creating the RFC to extend emergency credit to financial institutions and other eligible borrowers.

records.title: Banking Act expands Fed lending
records.policyGoal: The Banking Act of 1932 expands eligible lending collateral and permits government securities to back Federal Reserve notes.

records.title: Congress proposes lame-duck amendment
records.policyGoal: Congress approved a constitutional amendment proposal moving the start of presidential and congressional terms earlier.

records.title: Senate opens Wall Street hearings
records.policyGoal: The Senate Banking and Currency Committee opened hearings on banking and stock exchange practices.

records.title: Twentieth Amendment ratified
records.policyGoal: The amendment moving presidential terms to January 20 and congressional terms to January 3 was ratified.

records.title: Congress proposes Prohibition repeal
records.policyGoal: Congress submitted an amendment repealing the Eighteenth Amendment for state ratification.

records.title: Emergency Banking Act enacted
records.policyGoal: Roosevelt signed emergency legislation to restore confidence and facilitate bank reopening.

records.title: Conservation relief legislation approved
records.policyGoal: Congress approved legislation authorizing conservation work as unemployment relief.

records.title: Federal Emergency Relief Act approved
records.policyGoal: Federal relief grants to states were authorized under the Federal Emergency Relief Act.

records.title: Agricultural Adjustment Act approved
records.policyGoal: Agricultural adjustment legislation seeks to stabilize farm prices and incomes by managing production.

records.title: Tennessee Valley Authority established
records.policyGoal: Roosevelt signed legislation creating the TVA to address flooding and power supply in the Tennessee Valley.

records.title: Federal securities legislation approved
records.policyGoal: Federal securities legislation introduced registration requirements for securities offerings.

records.title: National Industrial Recovery Act enacted
records.policyGoal: The NIRA authorizes industry codes and public works as instruments of recovery.

records.title: Prohibition repealed by Twenty-First Amendment
records.policyGoal: Ratification of the Twenty-First Amendment repealed constitutional Prohibition.

records.title: Gold Reserve Act enacted
records.policyGoal: The Gold Reserve Act authorizes the president to adjust the dollar's gold value.

records.title: Philippine independence framework approved
records.policyGoal: The Tydings-McDuffie Act provides a transitional framework for Philippine independence.

records.title: Securities Exchange Act signed
records.policyGoal: Roosevelt signed legislation creating the Securities and Exchange Commission to oversee securities markets.

records.policyGoal: The Communications Act creates the FCC to oversee radio, telephone and telegraph communications.

records.title: National Housing Act signed
records.policyGoal: Roosevelt signed the National Housing Act creating the Federal Housing Administration.
